batch_notes: (1) Three KNOWN FAILURE properties are of two different kinds: the strfmt/N-named properties and the two swash underflow tests are narrowed reproductions (fixed font / forced spec region, main properties exclude the region) and are tagged pin; sqlparser's hegel_bracket_quoted_identifier_roundtrip and strsim's hegel_sorensen_dice_matches_reference are the general properties that found their bug and were kept failing (strsim adds a one_of! branch forcing the shrunk counterexample), so they are not tagged pin. (2) rust/steel has zero extracted properties (README: 'no hegel tests found?') although its pins reference display_read_roundtrip_is_equal and 'the division properties'; all five steel attributions are therefore none even though steel/3's pin names its finder explicitly. Extraction problem, not a test-quality problem. (3) Two strfmt 'properties' draw nothing (doc_examples, sign_is_unspecified_is_not_inverted): example tests registered through the property harness. (4) Rubric gaps seen here: (a) 'no panic AND output within a bound' hybrids (swash normalized_coords_no_panic, glyph_metrics_finite_and_no_panic) sit between robustness and spec-postcondition; (b) 'resource exhaustion yields the documented error rather than a native crash' (starlark recursion) sits between robustness and rejection; (c) mathematical relations between two functions of the same library (statrs pdf = d/dx cdf, sum pmf = cdf, sf + cdf = 1, cdf monotone) sit between algebraic-law and internal-consistency, and I split them by whether the doc stresses independent implementations. (5) symphonia has no doc comments at all (all explanation is inside the bodies); statrs gates heavily through helper predicates (known_bug_zone, icdf_arg_is_known_broken, cdf_arg_is_known_broken) whose exact coverage is not visible in the batch, and its pins are deterministic #[test]s with explicit 'Found by X' text, which made attribution easy. (6) oracle:external / oracle:model tags were added only where the oracle is not already the primary category.
